decision: Use a pnpm monorepo with packages/engine, adapters, themes, renderer-pixi, audio and apps/web
rationale: Package boundaries make the engine/UI decoupling visible and lint-enforceable for provider reviewers
tradeoffs: More workspace/tooling setup than a single Vite app

decision: Render reels with PixiJS v8 (see ADR-0002)
rationale: Industry-standard WebGL renderer for slot studios; GPU batching, filters and HiDPI out of the box
tradeoffs: ~200KB gzipped dependency; WebGL context-loss handling is our responsibility

decision: Pure engine package with ports (OutcomeProvider, ReelsPort, Clock, Rng); React only in apps/web (ADR-0001)
rationale: Deterministic, Node-testable game logic; renderer/UI/backend are swappable
tradeoffs: Port contracts must be designed up front; slight indirection from click to reel

decision: Table-driven reducer with effect descriptors, spinId stale-response guard, rejected events recorded not thrown (ADR-0003)
rationale: Makes double-spins and stale responses impossible and every transition inspectable
tradeoffs: Adding states requires table + test updates

decision: Server-authoritative OutcomeProvider port returning a discriminated union; MockProvider with latency/error injection and forced scenarios (ADR-0004)
rationale: Client code mirrors production against a real RGS; QA can force edge cases deterministically
tradeoffs: Mock 'server' logic ships in the demo bundle

decision: Single validated GameConfig drives layout, maths, paytable and theme tokens (ADR-0005)
rationale: New titles become data; paytable can never drift from maths
tradeoffs: Exotic mechanics need future engine extension points

decision: Ban enum/interface via ESLint no-restricted-syntax; money as integer minor units; even integer line-heights
rationale: Explicit union types and as-const objects are tree-shakeable and erase cleanly; integer cents avoid float drift

decision: Tune paytables by Monte-Carlo to ~95% RTP (neon-relic 95.1%, crystal-ways 94.5%) and gate configs in CI with simulate() bounds 85-105%
rationale: Unbalanced demo maths (51%/147%) would make the demo feel broken; a CI sim catches config regressions
tradeoffs: Estimated RTP only (40k spins, ±~2%); not a certified maths model

decision: Client-side request timeout (8s) synthesises a TIMEOUT error; late responses are rejected by state/spinId guards; balance resynced via provider.getBalance() on RECOVER
rationale: Prevents a hung request from wedging the round and keeps the displayed balance authoritative after errors
tradeoffs: Server may have settled a timed-out spin; we rely on balance resync rather than round replay

decision: Slam-stop is context-aware: queued in SPIN_REQUESTED, quick-stop in SPINNING, skip in STOPPING, skip presentation in WIN_PRESENTATION; spin button stops autoplay first
rationale: Matches player expectations across providers; one input never causes two state changes
tradeoffs: Players must press twice to both stop autoplay and slam the current spin

decision: Engine tsconfig targets ES2022 without DOM lib; timers reached through a typed globalThis host in clock.ts only
rationale: Compiler-level proof that the engine has no DOM dependency, beyond the lint rule
